metadata.title: Low-Rank Matrix Recovery from Row-and-Column Affine Measurements

extraction_notes.note: Arithmetic slip: with sigma_1=(sqrt2+1)n/3 and sigma_2=(sqrt2-1)n/3 the nuclear norm of X_0 is 2*sqrt2*n/3 (about 0.94n), not n*sqrt2/3 as written; the conclusion ||X_0||_* < ||X||_* = n still holds.
The rank estimator is printed as round((r^(C)+r^(C))/2); the text says it averages r^(C) and r^(R), so the second term should be r^(R).

In the proof of Theorem 3 the final bounds (bound_A2), (bound_A3) are stated as C_2||Z^(C)||_2 and C_3||Z^(R)||_2, dropping the sqrt(r/k) factor derived just before them and required by the theorem; there is also a stray fragment '$>1-e^{-c_3k}$.' before (bound_A3).

Proof of Lemma 6 sets gamma=-log(2)/K, which is negative (should be log(2)/K); the proof of Lemma 4 says 'gamma as in Theorem 4' but gamma is defined in Lemma 6; Talagrand's bound is printed with log(1+t/(sigma+Br)), where r looks like a typo (the standard form has B*E(Z) there).

Minor typos: probability '1-e^{nt^2/2}' (sign missing) in the proof of Corollary 2; 'N(0, sigma I_n)' for the covariance (sigma^2) in Lemma 3's proof; 'p{-1}' in (22); Z^(R) is declared n_1 x k^(R) and Z^(C) k^(C) x n_2, transposed relative to A^(R)X and XA^(C).

Section 4.1.2 says RCMC rows and columns are 'sampled with replacement', but the model of Section 2 (and Theorem 2's proof) is independent Bernoulli inclusion, i.e. without replacement. The Discussion calls recovery guarantees for RCMC a future challenge although Theorem 2 proves noiseless RCMC recovery; OpenP1 reads it as the noisy case.

Claim 1's proof appeals to B^(C)_(r) being closest in Frobenius norm but bounds the spectral-norm distance (Eckart-Young holds for both, so the step is fine but the stated reason does not match). In the Halko et al. algorithm, step 2 'argmin_C ||Q^(C)B^(C) - C Q^(R)T B^(R)T||' is dimensionally inconsistent as printed (Q^(C)T is presumably meant).

Lemma 3 (rotation invariance of Gaussian matrices) is a standard fact but the paper proves it without attribution, so kept origin paper; Lemma 6 is attributed to Candes & Recht (Thm 4.2) and re-proved, so it is external with a paper proof.

The set-up of the proof of Theorem 3 sits in running text before Lemma 8, outside any proof environment; it was split into definitions, a w.l.o.g. assumption and two claims used by the proofs. SVLS_P is a one-display modification of SVLS and gets no steps.

nodes.name: Matrix representation of an affine transformation
nodes.statement: In general, we can represent any affine transformation $\mathcal{{A}}$ in matrix representation $\mathcal{{A}}(X)=Avec(X)$, where $vec(X)$ is a column vector obtained by stacking all columns of $X$ on top of each other.

nodes.name: Measurement sparsity
nodes.statement: We concentrate on two properties: (i) storage required in order to represent the measurement operator, and (ii) measurement sparsity, defined as the sum over all measurements of the number of matrix entries participating in each measurement, that is $S(\mathcal{{A}})=||vec(A)||_0$.
nodes.statement_short: Measurement sparsity $S(\mathcal{A})=||vec(A)||_0$: total number of matrix entries entering all measurements.

nodes.name: Gaussian Ensemble (GE)
nodes.statement: In the Gaussian Ensemble model, the entries of the matrix $A$ in the matrix representation $\mathcal{{A}}(X)=Avec(X)$ are i.i.d. Gaussian random variables, $A_{ij} \sim N(0,1)$.
also_stated_at: It is instructive to compare our GRC ensemble to the Gaussian Ensemble (GE) \cite{candes2011tight}, with the matrix representation $\mathcal{{A}}(X)=Avec(X)$ where $A\in\matrixspace{d}{n_{1}n_{2}}$ and $A\overset{i.i.d.}{\sim} N(0,1)$.

nodes.name: Low-rank recovery in the Gaussian Ensemble from O(r(n1+n2)) measurements
nodes.statement: For this ensemble, one can recover uniquely a low rank matrix $X$ with $O(r (n_{1}+n_{2}))$ noiseless measurements using nuclear norm minimization \cite{recht2010guaranteed,candes2011tight} or other methods such as Singular Value Projection (SVP) \cite{jain2010guaranteed}, which is optimal up to constants.
nodes.origin_citation: Recht, Fazel & Parrilo 2010; Candes & Plan 2011; Jain et al. 2010 (SVP)
assumptions: For this ensemble
conclusions: one can recover uniquely a low rank matrix $X$ with $O(r (n_{1}+n_{2}))$ noiseless measurements
nodes.statement_short: In GE, nuclear norm minimization or SVP recovers a rank-$r$ matrix from $O(r(n_1+n_2))$ noiseless measurements.

nodes.name: Matrix completion needs Theta(n r log n) measurements
nodes.statement: However, recovery guarantees for this model are weaker: setting $n=\max(n_1,n_2)$, it is shown that $\Theta(nrlog(n))$ measurements are required to recover a rank $r$ matrix of size $n_1 \times n_2$ \cite{candes2010power}.
conclusions: $\Theta(nrlog(n))$ measurements are required to recover a rank $r$ matrix of size $n_1 \times n_2$
nodes.statement_short: Standard matrix completion needs $\Theta(nr\log n)$ uniformly sampled entries for a rank-$r$ matrix.

nodes.name: Rank one projections design
nodes.statement: Recently a new design of rank one projections was proposed \cite{cai2015rop}, where each measurement is of the form $\alpha^{T}X\beta$ and such that $\alpha\in\mathbb{R}^{n_{1}} , \beta\in\mathbb{R}^{n_{2}}$ have i.i.d standard Gaussian entries.
nodes.statement_short: Each measurement is $\alpha^TX\beta$ with i.i.d. standard Gaussian $\alpha,\beta$.

nodes.name: Nuclear norm recovery from rank one projections
nodes.statement: It was proven that nuclear norm minimization can recover $X$ with high probability in this design from $O(n_1r+n_2r)$ measurements.
conclusions: nuclear norm minimization can recover $X$ with high probability in this design from $O(n_1r+n_2r)$ measurements

nodes.name: Matrix spaces $\mathbb{R}_{n_1\times n_2}$, $\mathcal{O}_{n_1\times n_2}$, $\mathcal{M}^{(r)}_{n_1\times n_2}$
nodes.statement: We denote by $\matrixspace{n_{1}}{n_{2}}$ the space of matrices of size $n_{1}\times n_{2}$, by $\orthomatrixspace{n_{1}}{n_{2}}$ the space of matrices of size $n_{1}\times n_{2}$ with orthonormal columns, and by $\lowrank{n_{1}}{n_{2}}r$ the space of matrices of size $n_{1}\times n_{2}$ and rank $\leqslant r$.

nodes.name: $n=\max(n_1,n_2)$
nodes.statement: We denote $n=\max(n_1,n_2)$.

nodes.name: Frobenius, nuclear and spectral norms
nodes.statement: We denote by $||\cdot||_{F}$ the matrix Frobenius norm, by $||\cdot||_{*}$ the nuclear norm, and by $||\cdot||_{2}$ the spectral norm.

nodes.name: Vector $l_2$ norm
nodes.statement: For a vector, $||\cdot||$ denotes the standard $l_{2}$ norm.

nodes.name: Column span $span(X)$ and projection $P_X$
nodes.statement: For $X\in\matrixspace{n_{1}}{n_{2}}$we denote by $span(X)$ the subspace of $\mathbb{R}^{n_{1}}$ spanned by the columns of $X$ and define $P_{X}$ to be the orthogonal projection into $span(X)$.

nodes.name: Row, column and entry notation
nodes.statement: For a matrix $X$ we denote by $\matrixrow Xi$ the $i$-th row, by $\matrixcolumn Xj$ the $j$-th column and by $X_{ij}$ the $(i,j)$ element.

nodes.name: Sub-matrix $X_{IJ}$
nodes.statement: For two sets of indices $I,J$, we denote by $X_{IJ}$ the sub-matrix obtained by taking the rows with indices in $I$ and columns with indices in $J$ of $X$.

nodes.name: Index set $[k]$
nodes.statement: We denote by $[k]$ the set of indices $1,..,k$.

nodes.name: Vectorization $vec(X)$
nodes.statement: We denote by $vec(X)$ the (column) vector obtained by stacking all the columns of $X$ on top of each other.

nodes.name: i.i.d. random matrix notation
nodes.statement: We use the notation $X\overset{i.i.d.}{\sim} G$ to denote a random matrix $X$ with i.i.d. entries $X_{ij}\sim G$.

nodes.name: Singular Value Decomposition (SVD)
nodes.statement: For a rank-$r$ matrix $X\in\lowrank{n_{1}}{n_{2}}r$ let $X=U\Sigma V^{T}$ be the Singular Value Decomposition ($SVD$) where $U\in\orthomatrixspace{n_{1}}r,\thinspace V\in\orthomatrixspace r{n_{2}}$ and $\Sigma=diag(\sigma_{1}(X),...,\sigma_{r}(X))$ with $\sigma_{1}(X)\geq\sigma_{2}(X)\geq..\geq\sigma_{r}(X)>0$ the (non-zero) singular values of $X$ (we omit the zero singular values and their corresponding vectors from the decomposition).
nodes.statement_short: Compact SVD $X=U\Sigma V^T$ of a rank-$r$ matrix with only the $r$ non-zero singular values.

nodes.name: Top-r SVD $X_{(r)}$
nodes.statement: For a general matrix $X\in\matrixspace{n_{1}}{n_{2}}$ we denote by $\svdtop Xr$ the top-$r$ singular value decomposition of $X$, $\svdtop Xr=U_{\bullet[r]}\Sigma_{[r][r]}V_{\bullet[r]}^{T}$.

nodes.name: Row-and-column affine measurements $B^{(C,0)}=XA^{(C)}$, $B^{(R,0)}=A^{(R)}X$
nodes.statement: Our model assumes two affine transformations applied to $X$, representing rows and columns, $B^{(C,0)}=XA^{(C)}$ and $B^{(R,0)}=A^{(R)} X,$ achieved by multiplications with two matrices $A^{(R)}\in\matrixspace{k^{(R)}}{n_{1}}$ and $A^{(C)}\in\matrixspace{n_{2}}{k^{(C)}}$, respectively.
nodes.statement_short: The measurements are $B^{(C,0)}=XA^{(C)}$ and $B^{(R,0)}=A^{(R)}X$: linear combinations of columns and of rows of $X$.

nodes.name: Noisy observations $B^{(R)},B^{(C)}$ and number of measurements $d$
nodes.statement: We obtain noisy observations of these transformations, $B^{(R)},B^{(C)}$ obtained by applying additive noise: \begin{equation} A^{(R)} X+Z^{(R)}=B^{(R)}\,;\quad XA^{(C)}+Z^{(C)}=B^{(C)} \end{equation} where the total number of measurements is $d=k^{(R)}n_{1}+n_{2}k^{(C)}$, and $Z^{(R)}\in\mathbb{R}_{n_{1}\times k^{(R)}}$,$Z^{(C)}\in\mathbb{R}_{k^{(C)}\times n_{2}}$ are two zero-mean noise matrices.
nodes.statement_short: Observations $B^{(R)}=A^{(R)}X+Z^{(R)}$, $B^{(C)}=XA^{(C)}+Z^{(C)}$ with zero-mean noise; $d=k^{(R)}n_1+n_2k^{(C)}$ measurements.

nodes.name: Rank-constrained least-squares recovery
nodes.statement: To achieve this goal, we define the squared loss function \begin{equation} \mathcal{\mathcal{\mathcal{{F}}}}(X)=||A^{(R)} X-B^{(R)}||_{F}^{2}+||XA^{(C)}-B^{(C)}||_{F}^{2} \end{equation} and solve the least squares problem: \begin{equation} Minimize\:\mathcal{\mathcal{{F}}}(X)\: s.t.\: X\in\lowrank{n_{1}}{n_{2}}r. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Minimize the squared loss $\mathcal{F}(X)$ of row and column measurements over matrices of rank at most $r$.

nodes.name: Least squares is maximum likelihood under Gaussian noise
nodes.statement: If $Z^{(R)},Z^{(C)}\overset{i.i.d.}{\sim} N(0,\tau^{2})$ , minimizing the loss function in eq. (\ref{eq:losses_function}) is equivalent to maximizing the log-likelihood of the data, giving a statistical motivation for the above score.
assumptions: If $Z^{(R)},Z^{(C)}\overset{i.i.d.}{\sim} N(0,\tau^{2})$
conclusions: minimizing the loss function in eq. (\ref{eq:losses_function}) is equivalent to maximizing the log-likelihood of the data

nodes.name: Row and Column Matrix Completion (RCMC) ensemble
nodes.statement: \textbf{Row and Column Matrix Completion (RCMC):} In this ensemble each row of $A^{(R)}$ and each column of $A^{(C)}$ is a vector of the standard basis $e_{j}$ for some $j$ - thus each measurement $B^{(R)}_{ij}$ or $B^{(C)}_{ij}$is obtained from a single entry of $X$.
differentia: each row of $A^{(R)}$ and each column of $A^{(C)}$ is a vector of the standard basis $e_{j}$ for some $j$

nodes.name: Row and column inclusion probabilities $p^{(R)},p^{(C)}$
nodes.statement: We define a row-inclusion probability $p^{(R)}$ and column inclusion probability $p^{(C)}$ such that each row (column) of $X$ will be measured with probability $p^{(R)}$ ($p^{(C)}$).

nodes.name: Row-inclusion Bernoulli variables $r_i$
nodes.statement: More precisely, we define $r_{1},..,r_{n_{1}}$ i.i.d. Bernoulli variables, $P(r_{i}=1)=p^{(R)}$, and include $e_{i}$ as a row in $A^{(R)}$ if and only if $r_{i}=1$.

nodes.name: Column-inclusion Bernoulli variables $c_i$
nodes.statement: Similarly, we define $c_{1}...c_{n_{2}}$ i.i.d. Bernoulli variables, $P(c_{i}=1)=p^{(C)}$, and include $e_{i}$ as a column in $A^{(C)}$ if and only if $c_{i}=1$.

nodes.name: Gaussian Rows and Columns (GRC) ensemble
nodes.statement: \textbf{Gaussian Rows and Columns (GRC):} In this ensemble $A^{(R)},A^{(C)}\overset{i.i.d.}{\sim} N(0,1)$. Each observation $B^{(R)}_{ij}$ or $B^{(C)}_{ij}$ is obtained by a weighted sum of a single row or column of $X$, with i.i.d. Gaussian weights.

nodes.name: r-Restricted Isometry Property (r-RIP)
nodes.statement: (r-RIP) Let $\mathcal{{A}}:\matrixspace{n_{1}}{n_{2}}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}^{d}$ be a linear map. For every integer $r$ with $1\le r\le min(n_{1},n_{2})$, define the $r$-Restricted Isometry Constant to be the smallest number $\epsilon_{r}$ such that \begin{equation} (1-\epsilon_{r})||X||_{F}\leq ||\mathcal{{A}}(X)|| \leq(1+\epsilon_{r})||X||_{F} \end{equation} holds for all matrices $X$ of rank at most $r$.

nodes.name: The Gaussian Ensemble satisfies r-RIP
nodes.statement: The GE model satisfies the $r$-RIP condition for $d = O(rn)$ with high probability \cite{recht2010guaranteed}.
assumptions: $d = O(rn)$
conclusions: The GE model satisfies the $r$-RIP condition

nodes.name: GRC does not satisfy RIP; nuclear norm minimization fails
nodes.statement: Unlike GE, in our GRC model $\mathcal{{A}}(X)$ doesn't satisfy the $r$-RIP, and nuclear norm minimization fails.
conclusions: in our GRC model $\mathcal{{A}}(X)$ doesn't satisfy the $r$-RIP, and nuclear norm minimization fails

nodes.name: GRC preserves Frobenius norm of any low-rank matrix
nodes.statement: Instead, $A^{(R)},A^{(C)}$ preserve matrix Frobenius norm in high probability - a weaker property which holds for \textit{any} low-rank matrix. (see Lemma \ref{lem:JL_Lemma} in the Appendix).
also_stated_at: Representing the vectors in $Q$ as a matrix, Lemma \ref{lem:JL_Lemma} shows that $A^{(R)},A^{(C)}$ preserve matrix Frobenius norm with high probability - a weaker property than the RIP which holds for \textit{any} low-rank matrix.

nodes.name: Coherence of a subspace (Incoherence)
nodes.statement: (Incoherence). Let $U$ be a subspace of $\mathbb{R}^{n}$ of dimension $r$, and $P_{U}$ be the orthogonal projection on $U$. Then the coherence of $U$ (with respect to the standard basis $\{e_{i}\}$) is defined as \begin{equation} \text{\ensuremath{\mu}}(U)\text{\ensuremath{\equiv}}\frac{n}{r}max_{i}||P_{U}(e_{i})||^{2}. \end{equation}
nodes.label: def:-(Incoherence)

nodes.name: $\mu$-incoherent matrix
nodes.statement: We say that a matrix $X\in\matrixspace{n_{1}}{n_{2}}$ is $\mu$-incoherent if for the $SVD$ $X=U\Sigma V^{T}$ we have $max(\mu(U),\mu(V))\leq\mbox{\ensuremath{\mu}}$.

nodes.name: Nuclear norm minimization fails for RCMC
nodes.statement: However, nuclear norm minimization fails for the RCMC design, even when the matrix $X$ is incoherent, as shown by the next example:
conclusions: nuclear norm minimization fails for the RCMC design, even when the matrix $X$ is incoherent

nodes.name: All-ones matrix where nuclear norm minimization fails under RCMC
nodes.statement: Take $X\in\matrixspace nn$ for $\frac{n}{3}\in\mathbb{N}$ with $X_{ij}=1,\:\:\forall(i,j)\in[n]\times[n]$. Thus $||X||_{*}=n$. Take $k^{(R)}=k^{(C)}=\frac{n}{3}$. Set all unknown entries to $0.5$, giving a matrix $X_{0}$ of rank $2$ with $\sigma_{1}(X_{0})=\frac{(\sqrt{2}+1)n}{3}$, $\sigma_{2}(X_{0})=\frac{(\sqrt{2}-1)n}{3}$. Therefore $||X_{0}||_{*}=\frac{n\sqrt{2}}{3}<||X||_{*}$ and nuclear norm minimization fails to recover the correct $X$.
nodes.statement_short: For the all-ones $n\times n$ matrix with $n/3$ observed rows and columns, filling the rest with 0.5 gives smaller nuclear norm.

nodes.name: Noiseless recovery algorithm (Algorithm 1)
nodes.statement: Input: $A^{(R)},A^{(C)},B^{(R)},B^{(C)}$ and rank $r$ \begin{enumerate} \item Compute a basis (of size $r$) to the column space of $B^{(C)}$ using Gaussian elimination, represented as the columns of a matrix $\hat{U} \in \matrixspace {n_{1}}r $. \item Solve the linear system $B_{\bullet j}^{(R)}=A^{(R)}\hat{U}Y_{\bullet j}$ for each $j=1,..,n_2$ and write the solutions as a matrix $Y=Y_{\bullet1}...Y_{\bullet n_{2}}$. \item Output $\hat{X}=\hat{U}Y$ \end{enumerate} \protect\caption{}
nodes.statement_short: Take a basis $\hat{U}$ of the column space of $B^{(C)}$, solve $B^{(R)}=A^{(R)}\hat{U}Y$ by least squares, output $\hat{U}Y$.
nodes.label: alg:noiseless_case

nodes.name: Closed form of the Algorithm 1 estimator
nodes.statement: If $rank(A^{(R)}\hat{U})=r$ one can write the resulting estimator $\hat{X}$ in closed-form as follows: \begin{equation} \hat{X}=\hat{U}Y=\hat{U}[\hat{U}^{T}A^{(R)^{T}}A^{(R)}\hat{U}]^{-1}\hat{U}^{T}A^{(R)^{T}}B^{(R)} \end{equation}
assumptions: If $rank(A^{(R)}\hat{U})=r$

nodes.name: Column version of the closed-form estimator
nodes.statement: We can apply the same algorithm, but changing the role of rows and columns. The resulting closed form solution is then: \begin{equation} \hat{X}=B^{(C)}A^{(C)}\hat{V}[\hat{V}^{T}A^{(C)}A^{(C)^{T}}\hat{V}]^{-1}\hat{V}^{T} \end{equation} for an orthogonal matrix $\hat{V}$ representing a basis for the rows of $X$.

nodes.name: SVLS (Singular Value Least Squares)
nodes.statement: Input: $A^{(R)},A^{(C)},B^{(R)},B^{(C)}$ and rank $r$ \begin{enumerate} \item Compute $\hat{U}$, the $r$ largest left singular vectors of $B^{(C)}$, ($\hat{U}$ is a basis for the columns space of $B^{(C)}_{(r)}$). \item Find the least-squares solution \begin{equation} \hat{Y}=argmin_{Y}\parallel B^{(R)}-A^{(R)}\hat{U}Y||_F. \end{equation} If $rank(A^{(R)}\hat{U})=r$ we can write $\hat{Y}$ in closed form as before: \begin{equation} \hat{Y}=[\hat{U}^{T}A^{(R)^{T}}A^{(R)}\hat{U}]^{-1}\hat{U}^{T}A^{(R)^{T}}B^{(R)}. \end{equation} \item Compute the estimate $\hat{X}^{(R)}=\hat{U}\hat{Y}$. \item Repeat steps 1-3, replacing the roles of columns and rows to get an estimate $\hat{X}^{(C)}$. \item Set $\hat{X} = argmin_{\hat{X}^{(R)},\hat{X}^{(C)}} \mathcal{\mathcal{{F}}}(X)$, for the loss $\mathcal{\mathcal{{F}}}(X)$ given in eq. (\ref{eq:losses_function}). \end{enumerate} \protect\caption{ SVLS}
nodes.statement_short: Top-$r$ left singular vectors of $B^{(C)}$ give $\hat{U}$; least squares on row measurements gives $\hat{U}\hat{Y}$; do the symmetric version, keep the lower-loss estimate.
nodes.label: alg:basis_noisy_case

nodes.name: Gradient descent refinement in factored form
nodes.statement: The gradient descent stage is performed directly in the space of rank $r$ matrices, using the decomposition $\hat{X}$=$WS$ where $W\in\matrixspace{n_{1}}r$ and $S\in\matrixspace r{n_{2}}$ and computing the gradient of the loss as a function of $W$ and $S$, \begin{equation} \mathcal{\mathcal{{L}}}(W,S) = \mathcal{\mathcal{{F}}}(WS) = ||A^{(R)} WS-B^{(R)}||_{F}^{2} + ||WSA^{(C)}-B^{(C)}||_{F}^{2}. \end{equation} We want to minimize eq. (\ref{eq:loss_function_W_S}) but the loss $\mathcal{\mathcal{{L}}}$ isn't convex and therefore gradient descent may fail to converge to a global optimum. We propose $\hat{X}$ (the output of SVLS\!) as a starting point which may be close enough to enable gradient descent to converge to the global optimum, and in addition may accelerate convergence. The gradient of $\mathcal{\mathcal{{L}}}$ is (using the chain rule) $$ \frac{\partial \mathcal{\mathcal{{L}}}}{\partial W}= 2 \Big[ A^{(R)^{T}}(A^{(R)} WS-B^{(R)})S^{T}+(WSA^{(C)}-B^{(C)})A^{(C)^{T}}S^{T} \Big] $$ \begin{equation} \frac{\partial \mathcal{\mathcal{{L}}}}{\partial S}= 2 \Big[ W^{T}A^{(R)^{T}}(A^{(R)} WS-B^{(R)})+W^{T}(WSA^{(C)}-B^{(C)})A^{(C)^{T}} \Big] \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Gradient descent on $\mathcal{L}(W,S)=\mathcal{F}(WS)$ over the factors, started from the SVLS estimate.

nodes.name: Elbow-method rank estimator
nodes.statement: For the noisy case we estimate $rank(X)$ from $B^{(C)},B^{(R)}$. We use the popular elbow method to estimate $rank(B^{(C)})$ in the following way \begin{equation} \hat{r}^{(C)}=argmax_{i\in[k^{(C)}-1]}\left(\frac{\sigma_{i}(B^{(C)})}{\sigma_{i+1}(B^{(C)})}\right) \end{equation} We compute similarly $\hat{r}^{(R)}$ from $B^{(R)}$ and take the average as our rank estimator, $\hat{r}=round\left(\frac{\hat{r}^{(C)}+\hat{r}^{(C)}}{2}\right)$.
nodes.statement_short: Estimate the rank of each of $B^{(C)},B^{(R)}$ by the largest ratio of consecutive singular values, then average.

nodes.name: Low rank matrix approximation problem
nodes.statement: In the low rank matrix approximation problem, the goal is to approximate a (possibly full rank) matrix $X$ by the closest (in Frobenius norm) rank-$r$ matrix $X_{(r)}$.

nodes.name: Eckart-Young Theorem
nodes.statement: By the Eckart-Young Theorem \cite{eckart1936approximation}, this problem has a closed-form solution which is the truncated $SVD$ of $X$.
conclusions: this problem has a closed-form solution which is the truncated $SVD$ of $X$

nodes.name: $SVLS_P$ (SVLS with Halko-Martinsson-Tropp projections)
nodes.statement: We adjusted the algorithm presented in \cite{halko2011finding} to our problem and give a new estimator which is a combination of SVLS and \cite{halko2011finding}'s method, replacing $\hat{X}^{(R)}$ and $\hat{X}^{(C)}$ in steps 3,4 of SVLS by: \begin{equation} \quad \hat{X}^{(R)}_{P}=\hat{X}^{(R)}\hat{V}\hat{V}^T \:, \quad \hat{X}^{(C)}_{P}=\hat{U}\hat{U}^T\hat{X}^{(C)}. \end{equation} Here $\hat{V}$ is the $r$ largest right singular vectors of $B^{(R)}$ and $\hat{U}$ is the $r$ largest left singular vectors of $B^{(C)}$. We call this new estimator $SVLS_P$.
nodes.statement_short: SVLS whose two estimates are additionally projected on the top-$r$ singular subspaces of $B^{(R)}$ and $B^{(C)}$.

nodes.name: Degrees of freedom of a rank-r matrix
nodes.statement: A rank $r$ matrix of size $n_{1}\times n_{2}$ has $r(n_{1}+n_{2}-r)$ degrees of freedom, and can therefore not be uniquely recovered by fewer measurements.
conclusions: has $r(n_{1}+n_{2}-r)$ degrees of freedom, and can therefore not be uniquely recovered by fewer measurements

nodes.name: Uniqueness from row and column measurements
nodes.statement: Let $X_{1},X_{2}\in\lowrank{n_{1}}{n_{2}}r$ and $A^{(R)}\in\matrixspace{k^{(R)}}{n_{1}},A^{(C)}\in\matrixspace{n_{2}}{k^{(C)}}$ such that $rank(A^{(R)}X_{1})=rank(X_{1}A^{(C)})=r$. If $A^{(R)}X_{1}=A^{(R)}X_{2}$ and $X_{1}A^{(C)}=X_{2}A^{(C)}$ then $X_{1}=X_{2}$.
assumptions: Let $X_{1},X_{2}\in\lowrank{n_{1}}{n_{2}}r$ and $A^{(R)}\in\matrixspace{k^{(R)}}{n_{1}},A^{(C)}\in\matrixspace{n_{2}}{k^{(C)}}$ such that $rank(A^{(R)}X_{1})=rank(X_{1}A^{(C)})=r$
nodes.statement_short: Two rank-$r$ matrices agreeing on full-rank row and column measurements are equal.
nodes.label: lem:uniqness solution affine

nodes.name: Algorithm 1 output agrees with the measurements
nodes.statement: Let $X\in\lowrank{n_{1}}{n_{2}}r$ and $A^{(R)}\in\matrixspace{k^{(R)}}{n_{1}},A^{(C)}\in\matrixspace{n_{2}}{k^{(C)}}$ such that $rank(A^{(R)} X)=rank(XA^{(C)})=r$. For Algorithm \ref{alg:noiseless_case} with inputs $A^{(R)},A^{(C)},B^{(R,0)},$ $B^{(C,0)}$ and $r$ the output $\hat{X}$ satisfies \begin{equation} A^{(R)}X=A^{(R)}\hat{X},\, XA^{(C)}=\hat{X}A^{(C)} \end{equation}
assumptions: Let $X\in\lowrank{n_{1}}{n_{2}}r$ and $A^{(R)}\in\matrixspace{k^{(R)}}{n_{1}},A^{(C)}\in\matrixspace{n_{2}}{k^{(C)}}$ such that $rank(A^{(R)} X)=rank(XA^{(C)})=r$
conclusions: the output $\hat{X}$ satisfies
nodes.statement_short: With full-rank noiseless measurements, the Algorithm 1 output reproduces both $A^{(R)}X$ and $XA^{(C)}$.
nodes.label: lem:hatX_is_X

nodes.name: Exact recovery for GRC with minimal measurements
nodes.statement: Let $\hat{X}$ be the output of Algorithm \ref{alg:noiseless_case} in the GRC model with $Z^{(C)},Z^{(R)}=0$ and $k^{(R)},k^{(C)}\geq r$. Then $P(\hat{X}=X)=1$.
assumptions: Let $\hat{X}$ be the output of Algorithm \ref{alg:noiseless_case} in the GRC model with $Z^{(C)},Z^{(R)}=0$ and $k^{(R)},k^{(C)}\geq r$
nodes.statement_short: In noiseless GRC with $k^{(R)},k^{(C)}\ge r$, Algorithm 1 recovers $X$ with probability 1.
nodes.label: cor:uniqness_GRC

nodes.name: Exact recovery for RCMC with high probability
nodes.statement: Let $X=U\Sigma V^{T}$ be the $SVD$ of $X \in \matrixspace {n_1}{n_2}$, and $\max(\mu(U),\mu(V))<\mu$. Take $A^{(R)}$ and $A^{(C)}$ as in the RCMC model without noise and probabilities $p^{(R)}=\frac{k}{n_1}$ and $p^{(C)}=\frac{k}{n_2}$. Let $\beta>1$ such that $C_{R}\sqrt{\frac{\beta log(n)r\mu}{k}}<1$ where $C_{R}$ is uniform constant and let $\hat{X}$ be the output of Algorithm \ref{alg:noiseless_case}. Then $P\left(\hat{X}=X\right)>1-6min(n_1,n_2)^{-\beta}$.
assumptions: Let $X=U\Sigma V^{T}$ be the $SVD$ of $X \in \matrixspace {n_1}{n_2}$, and $\max(\mu(U),\mu(V))<\mu$
Take $A^{(R)}$ and $A^{(C)}$ as in the RCMC model without noise and probabilities $p^{(R)}=\frac{k}{n_1}$ and $p^{(C)}=\frac{k}{n_2}$
Let $\beta>1$ such that $C_{R}\sqrt{\frac{\beta log(n)r\mu}{k}}<1$ where $C_{R}$ is uniform constant
conclusions: Then $P\left(\hat{X}=X\right)>1-6min(n_1,n_2)^{-\beta}$
nodes.statement_short: For $\mu$-incoherent $X$ and $k\gtrsim \beta\mu r\log n$ sampled rows and columns, Algorithm 1 recovers $X$ w.p. $>1-6\min(n_1,n_2)^{-\beta}$.
nodes.label: theorem:Uniqness_MC

nodes.name: Both row and column measurements are needed
nodes.statement: Both row and column measurements are need in order to guarantee unique recovery. If, for example, we observe only rows then even with $n-1$ observed rows and rank $r=1$ we can only determine the unobserved row up to a constant, and thus cannot recover $X$ uniquely.

nodes.name: Gaussian Ensemble noisy error bound
nodes.statement: In \cite{candes2011tight} it is shown for GE that $||X-\hat{X}||_{F}<C_{G}\sqrt{\frac{nr\tau^{2}}{d}}$ holds with high probability for some constant $C_{G}$.
conclusions: $||X-\hat{X}||_{F}<C_{G}\sqrt{\frac{nr\tau^{2}}{d}}$ holds with high probability for some constant $C_{G}$

nodes.name: Error bound for SVLS in the noisy GRC model
nodes.statement: Let $A^{(R)}$ and $A^{(C)}$ with $k\geq max(4r,40)$ be as in the GRC model with noise matrices $Z^{(R)},Z^{(C)}$. Let $\hat{X}$ be the output of SVLS. Then there exist constants $c,c^{(R)},c^{(C)}$ such that with probability $>1-5e^{-ck}$: \begin{equation} ||X-\hat{X}||_{F} \leq \sqrt{\frac{r}{k}} \Big[ c^{(C)} ||Z^{(C)}||_{2}+c^{(R)} ||Z^{(R)}||_{2} \Big]. \end{equation}
assumptions: Let $A^{(R)}$ and $A^{(C)}$ with $k\geq max(4r,40)$ be as in the GRC model with noise matrices $Z^{(R)},Z^{(C)}$
Let $\hat{X}$ be the output of SVLS
conclusions: there exist constants $c,c^{(R)},c^{(C)}$ such that with probability $>1-5e^{-ck}$:

(\ref{eq:matrix_singular_values}) we get $max(||Z^{(R)}||_{2},||Z^{(C)}||_{2}) \leq 4\tau \sqrt{n}$ with probability $1-e^{-2n}$. We therefore get the next Corollary for i.i.d. additive Gaussian noise:
nodes.statement_short: Plug the Gaussian spectral-norm bound $||Z||_2\le 4\tau\sqrt{n}$ (w.p. $1-e^{-2n}$) into Theorem 3.

nodes.name: Noisy GRC error bound for i.i.d. Gaussian noise
nodes.statement: Let $A^{(R)}$, $A^{(C)}$ as in the GRC with $n\geq k\geq max(4r,40)$, model and $Z^{(R)},Z^{(C)}\overset{i.i.d.}{\sim} N(0,\tau^{2})$. Then there exist constants $c,C_{GRC}$ such that: \begin{equation} P\Big(||X-\hat{X}||_{F}\leq C_{GRC} \sqrt{\frac{\tau^{2}nr}{k}}\Big) > 1-5e^{-ck}-e^{-2n} . \end{equation}
assumptions: Let $A^{(R)}$, $A^{(C)}$ as in the GRC with $n\geq k\geq max(4r,40)$, model and $Z^{(R)},Z^{(C)}\overset{i.i.d.}{\sim} N(0,\tau^{2})$
conclusions: there exist constants $c,C_{GRC}$ such that:

nodes.name: Relative Root-Mean-Squared-Error (RRMSE)
nodes.statement: We measured the reconstruction accuracy using the Relative Root-Mean-Squared-Error ($RRMSE$), defined as \begin{equation} RRMSE \equiv RRMSE(X,\hat{X}) \equiv ||X - \hat{X}||_{F}/||X||_{F}. \end{equation}

nodes.name: RCMC with SVLS reaches exact recovery at the optimal number of measurements
nodes.statement: SVLS recovers $X$ with probability $1$ with the optimal number of measurements $d=r(2n-r)=894$ yielding $\frac{d}{n^{2}}\approx0.04$ while MC with OptSpace and SVT need roughly $3$-fold and $8$-fold more measurements, respectively, to guarantee exact recovery.

nodes.name: SVLS is stable on RCMC while OptSpace and SVT are not
nodes.statement: Figure \ref{fig:algorithm_performance} shows that while the performance of SVLS is very stable even for small $k$, the performance of OptSpace varies, with multiple instances achieving poor accuracy, and SVT which minimizes the nuclear norm achieves poor accuracy for all problem instances.

nodes.name: OptSpace trimming step omitted for RCMC
nodes.statement: The OptSpace algorithm has a trimming step which delete dense columns. We omitted this step in the RCMC model since it would delete all the known columns and rows and it's not stable for this type of measurements, but it still get better result than SVT.

nodes.name: SVLS on RCMC is faster than and comparably accurate to MC algorithms
nodes.statement: Results, displayed in Table \ref{tab:accuracy-and-time}, show that SVLS is significantly faster than the other two algorithms. It is also more accurate than MC for small number of measurements, and comparable to MC for large number of measurements.

nodes.name: GRC outperforms GE at all noise levels
nodes.statement: For all noise levels, the performance of GRC was better than the performance of GE.

nodes.name: RRMSE decays at rate sqrt(k)
nodes.statement: The $RRMSE$ error decays at a rate of $\sqrt{k}$.

nodes.name: RRMSE is linear in the noise level
nodes.statement: The change in the relative error $RRMSE$ is linear in $\tau$ while the rate depends on $r$.

nodes.name: Scaled RRMSE is insensitive to n
nodes.statement: Results (shown in the Appendix, Section \ref{sec:appendix_simulations}) indicate that when properly scaled, the $RRMSE$ error is not sensitive to the value of $n$ and other parameters, in agreement with Theorem \ref{thm:the_noisy_case}.

nodes.name: Recovery guarantees for noisy RCMC
nodes.statement: For RCMC, our simulations show that the RCMC design may achieve comparable or favorable results, compared to the standard MC design, especially for low noise level. Proving recovery guarantees for this RCMC model is an interesting future challenge.
nodes.statement_short: Prove recovery guarantees for the RCMC design (beyond the noiseless case).

nodes.name: Rotation invariance of Gaussian matrices
nodes.statement: Let $V\in\orthomatrixspace nr$ and $A^{(C)}\in\matrixspace nk$ be a random matrix $A^{(C)}\overset{i.i.d.}{\sim} N(0,\sigma^{2})$. Then $V^{T}A^{(C)} \overset{i.i.d.}{\sim} N(0,\sigma^{2})$. \begin{proof} For any two matrices $A\in\matrixspace{n_{1}}{n_{2}}$ and $B\in\matrixspace{m_{1}}{m_{2}}$ we define their Kronecker product as a matrix in $\matrixspace{n_{1}m_{1}}{n_{2}m_{2}}$: \begin{equation} A\otimes B=\left( \begin{array}{ccccc} a_{11}B & a_{12}B & . & . & a_{1n_2}B \\ . & . & . & . & . \\ . & . & . & . & . \\ . & . & . & . & . \\ a_{n_1 1}B & a_{n_1 2}B & . & . & a_{n_1 n_2}B \\ \end{array} \right) \end{equation} Now, we have $vec(V^{T}A^{(C)})=(\identity n\otimes V^{T})vec(A^{(C)})$ and since $vec(A^{(C)})\sim N(0,\sigma \identity n)$ the vector $(\identity n\otimes V^{T})vec(A^{(C)})$ is also a multivariate Gaussian vector with zero mean and covariance matrix: \begin{align} COV \Big( V^{T}A^{(C)} \Big) = COV \Big( (\identity n\otimes V^{T})vec(A^{(C)}) \Big) = \nonumber \\ (\identity n\otimes V^{T})COV\left(vec(A^{(C)})\right)(\identity n\otimes V^{T})^{T}= \nonumber \\ \sigma^{2}(\identity n\otimes V^{T})(\identity n\otimes V^{T})^{T}=\sigma^{2}\identity r\otimes\identity n = \sigma^2 \identity {nr}. \end{align} \end{proof}
assumptions: Let $V\in\orthomatrixspace nr$ and $A^{(C)}\in\matrixspace nk$ be a random matrix $A^{(C)}\overset{i.i.d.}{\sim} N(0,\sigma^{2})$
conclusions: Then $V^{T}A^{(C)} \overset{i.i.d.}{\sim} N(0,\sigma^{2})$
nodes.statement_short: For $V$ with orthonormal columns and i.i.d. Gaussian $A$, $V^TA$ is again i.i.d. Gaussian.
nodes.label: lem:unitary_normal

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3
nodes.statement: For any two matrices $A\in\matrixspace{n_{1}}{n_{2}}$ and $B\in\matrixspace{m_{1}}{m_{2}}$ we define their Kronecker product as a matrix in $\matrixspace{n_{1}m_{1}}{n_{2}m_{2}}$: \begin{equation} A\otimes B=\left( \begin{array}{ccccc} a_{11}B & a_{12}B & . & . & a_{1n_2}B \\ . & . & . & . & . \\ . & . & . & . & . \\ . & . & . & . & . \\ a_{n_1 1}B & a_{n_1 2}B & . & . & a_{n_1 n_2}B \\ \end{array} \right) \end{equation} Now, we have $vec(V^{T}A^{(C)})=(\identity n\otimes V^{T})vec(A^{(C)})$ and since $vec(A^{(C)})\sim N(0,\sigma \identity n)$ the vector $(\identity n\otimes V^{T})vec(A^{(C)})$ is also a multivariate Gaussian vector with zero mean and covariance matrix: \begin{align} COV \Big( V^{T}A^{(C)} \Big) = COV \Big( (\identity n\otimes V^{T})vec(A^{(C)}) \Big) = \nonumber \\ (\identity n\otimes V^{T})COV\left(vec(A^{(C)})\right)(\identity n\otimes V^{T})^{T}= \nonumber \\ \sigma^{2}(\identity n\otimes V^{T})(\identity n\otimes V^{T})^{T}=\sigma^{2}\identity r\otimes\identity n = \sigma^2 \identity {nr}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Write $vec(V^TA)=(I\otimes V^T)vec(A)$ and compute its covariance via Kronecker products.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1
nodes.statement: Let $U\Sigma V^{T}$ be the $SVD$ of $X$. From Lemma \ref{lem:unitary_normal} the elements of the matrix $V^T A^{(C)}$ have a continuous Gaussian distribution and since the measure of low rank matrices is zero and $k^{(C)}\geq r$ we get that $P(rank(V^{T} A^{(C)})=r)=1$. Since $B^{(C)}=U\Sigma V^{T} A^{(C)}$ we get $P(rank(B^{(C)})=rank(U\Sigma V^{T} A^{(C)})=r)=1$. In the same way $P(rank(B^{(R)})=r)=1$. Combining Lemma \ref{lem:hatX_is_X} with Lemma \ref{lem:uniqness solution affine} give us the required result.
nodes.statement_short: By Lemma 3, $V^TA^{(C)}$ is Gaussian so has rank $r$ a.s.; then Lemmas 2 and 1 give $\hat{X}=X$.

nodes.name: Projection form of the RCMC spectral condition
nodes.statement: Because $U$ is orthonormal, this is equivalent to \begin{equation} p{-1} || UU^{T}A^{(R)^{T}}A^{(R)}UU^{T}-pUU^{T} ||_{2} < 1 \Leftrightarrow p^{-1} || P_{U}P_{A^{(R)^{T}}}P_{U}-p P_{U}||_{2}<1 \end{equation} where $P_{U}=UU^{T},P_{A^{(R)^{T}}}=A^{(R)^{T}}A^{(R)}$ and $p^{(R)}=p$.
nodes.statement_short: $p^{-1}||U^TA^TAU-pI_r||_2<1$ is equivalent to the same bound for $P_UP_{A^{(R)T}}P_U-pP_U$.

nodes.name: Spectral concentration for RCMC row sampling
nodes.statement: Suppose $A^{(R)}$ as in the RCMC model with inclusion probability $p$, and $U\in\orthomatrixspace {n_1}r$ with $\mu(U)=\frac{n_1}{r}max_{i}||P_{U}(e_{i})||^{2}=\mu$. Then there is a numerical constant $C_{R}$ such that for all $\beta>1$, if $C_{R}\sqrt{\frac{\beta log(n_1)r\mu}{pn_1}}<1$ then: \begin{equation} P\left(p^{-1}||P_{U}P_{A^{(R)^{T}}}P_{U}-pP_{U}||_{2}<C_{R}\sqrt{\frac{\beta log(n_1)r\mu}{pn_1}}\right) >1-3n_{1}^{-\beta} \end{equation}
assumptions: Suppose $A^{(R)}$ as in the RCMC model with inclusion probability $p$, and $U\in\orthomatrixspace {n_1}r$ with $\mu(U)=\frac{n_1}{r}max_{i}||P_{U}(e_{i})||^{2}=\mu$
if $C_{R}\sqrt{\frac{\beta log(n_1)r\mu}{pn_1}}<1$
conclusions: there is a numerical constant $C_{R}$ such that for all $\beta>1$
nodes.statement_short: Row sampling with probability $p$ keeps $p^{-1}P_UP_{A^{(R)T}}P_U$ within $C_R\sqrt{\beta\mu r\log n_1/(pn_1)}$ of $P_U$ w.p. $>1-3n_1^{-\beta}$.
nodes.label: lemma: uniqnes_MC

nodes.name: Expectation bound for Bernoulli sums of rank-one matrices (Rudelson-type)
nodes.statement: If $y_{i}$ is a family of vectors in $\mathbb{R}^{d}$ and ${r_{i}}$ is a sequence of i.i.d. Bernoulli random variables with $P(r_{i}=1)=p$, then \begin{equation} E \big(p^{-1} ||\Sigma_{i}(r_{i}-p)y_{i}\otimes y_{i}|| \big) < C\sqrt{\frac{log(d)}{p}}max_{i}||y_{i}|| \end{equation} for some numerical constant $C$ provided that the right hand side is less than $1$.
assumptions: If $y_{i}$ is a family of vectors in $\mathbb{R}^{d}$ and ${r_{i}}$ is a sequence of i.i.d. Bernoulli random variables with $P(r_{i}=1)=p$
provided that the right hand side is less than $1$
nodes.label: lem:expection_bound-1

nodes.name: Talagrand's concentration inequality
nodes.statement: Let $Y_{1}...Y_{n}$ be a sequence of independent random variables taking values in a Banach space and define \begin{equation} Z=sup_{f\in F}\sum_{i=1}^{n}f(Y_{i}) \end{equation} where $F$ is a real countable set of functions such that if $f\in F$ then $-f\in F$. Assume that $|f|\leq B$ and $E(f(Y_{i}))=0$ for every $f\in F$ and $i\in[n]$. Then there exists a constant $C$ such that for every $t\geq0$ \begin{equation} P\big(|Z-E(Z)|\geq t\big)\leq3exp\left(\frac{-t}{CB}log(1+\frac{t}{\sigma+Br})\right) \end{equation} where $\sigma=sup_{f\in F}\sum_{i=1}^{n}E(f^{2}(Y_{i}))$.
nodes.statement_short: Concentration of the supremum of a bounded, centered empirical process around its mean.
nodes.label: theorem: talngrad_inequality-1

nodes.name: Concentration of $||Y||_2$ for Bernoulli-sampled projections
nodes.statement: Let $U\in\orthomatrixspace nr$ with incoherence constant $\mu$. Let $r_i$ be i.i.d. Bernoulli random variables with $P(r_i=1)=p$ and let $Y_{i}=p^{-1}(r_{i}-p)P_{U}(e_{i})\otimes P_{U}(e_{i})$ for $i=1,..,n$. Let $Y=\sum_{i=1}^{n}Y_{i}$\textup{ and $Z=||Y||_{2}$. Suppose $E(Z)\leq 1$. Then for every $\lambda>0$ we have \begin{equation} P\Big(|Z-E(Z)|\geq\lambda\sqrt{\frac{\mu rlog(n)}{pn}}\Big)\leq3exp\Big(-\gamma min(\lambda^{2}log(n),\lambda\sqrt{\frac{pnlog(n)}{\mu r}})\Big) \end{equation} for some positive constant $\gamma$.}
nodes.statement_short: $Z=||\sum_i p^{-1}(r_i-p)P_U e_i\otimes P_U e_i||_2$ concentrates around its mean at scale $\sqrt{\mu r\log n/(pn)}$.
nodes.label: lem:bound_Z-1

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 6
nodes.statement: We know that $Z=||Y||_{2}=sup_{f_{1},f_{2}} \langle f_{1},Yf_{2} \rangle =sup_{f_{1},f_{2}}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\langle f_{1,}Y_{i}f_{2} \rangle$, where the supremum is taken over a countable set of unit vectors $f_{1},f_{2}\in F_{V}$. Let $F$ be the set of all functions $f$ such that $f(Y)= \langle f_{1},Yf_{2} \rangle$ for some unit vectors $f_{1},f_{2}\in F_{V}$. For every $f\in F$ and $i\in[n]$ we have $E(f(Y_{i}))=0$. From the incoherence of $U$ we conclude that \begin{equation} |f(Y_{i})| = p^{-1} |r_{i}-p| \times | \langle f_{1},P_{U}(e_{i}) \rangle | \times | \langle P_{U}(e_{i}),f_{2} \rangle | \leq p^{-1} ||P_{U}(e_{i})||^{2} \leq p^{-1}\frac{r}{n}\mu. \end{equation} In addition \[ E (f^{2}(Y_{i})) =p^{-1}(1-p) \langle f_{1},P_{U}(e_{i}) \rangle^{2} \langle P_{U}(e_{i}),f_{2} \rangle^{2} \leq \] \begin{equation} p^{-1}||P_{U}(e_{i})||^{2}| \langle P_{U}(e_{i}),f_{2} \rangle^2 |\leq p^{-1}\frac{r}{n}\mu| \langle P_{U}(e_{i}),f_{2} \rangle|^{2}. \end{equation} Since $\sum_{i=1}^{n}| \langle P_{U}(e_{i}),f_{2} \rangle|^{2}=\sum_{i=1}^{n}| \langle e_{i},P_{U}(f_{2}) \rangle |^{2}=||P_{U}(f_{2})||^{2} \leq 1$, we get $\sum_{i=1}^{n} E (f^{2}(Y_{i})) \leq p^{-1}\frac{r}{n}\mu.$ We can take $B=2p^{-1}\frac{r}{n}\mu$ and $t=\lambda\sqrt{\frac{\mu rlog(n)}{pn}}$ and from Theorem \ref{theorem: talngrad_inequality-1}: \begin{equation} P(|Z-E(Z)|\geq t) \leq 3exp\left(\frac{-t}{KB}log(1+\frac{t}{2})\right) \leq 3exp\left(\frac{-tlog(2)}{KB}min(1,\frac{t}{2})\right) \end{equation} where the last inequality is due to the fact that for every $u>0$ we have $log(1+u)\geq log(2)min(1,u)$. Taking $\gamma=-log(2)/K$ finishes our proof.
nodes.statement_short: Write $Z$ as a supremum of an empirical process, bound $|f|$ and the variance by incoherence, apply Talagrand's inequality.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4
nodes.statement: (Lemma \ref{lemma: uniqnes_MC}) Represent any vector $w\in R^{n_1}$ in the standard basis as $w=\sum_{i=1}^{n_1} \langle w,e_{i} \rangle e_{i}$. Therefore $P_{U}(w)=\sum_{i=1}^{n_1} \langle P_{U}(w),e_{i} \rangle e_{i}=\sum_{i=1}^{n_1} \langle w,P_{U}(e_{i}) \rangle e_{i}$. Recall the $r_i$ Bernoulli variables which determine if $e_i$ is included as a row of $A^{(R)}$ as in Section \ref{sec:Preliminaries-and-Notations} and define $Y_i$ and $Z$ as in Lemma \ref{lem:bound_Z-1}. We get \begin{align} P_{A^{(R)^{T}}}P_{U}(w)=\sum_{i=1}^{n_1}r_{i} \langle w,P_{U}(e_{i}) \rangle e_{i}\Longrightarrow \nonumber \\ P_{U}P_{A^{(R)^{T}}}P_{U}(w)=\sum_{i=1}^{n_1}r_{i} \langle w,P_{U}(e_{i}) \rangle P_{U}(e_{i}) \end{align} In other words the matrix $P_{U}P_{A^{(R)^{T}}}P_{U}$ is given by \begin{equation} P_{U}P_{A^{(R)^{T}}}P_{U} = \sum_{i=1}^{n_1} r_{i}P_{U}(e_{i})\otimes P_{U}(e_{i}) \end{equation} $U$ is $\mu-$incoherent, thus $max_{i\in[n_1]}||P_{U}(e_{i})||\leq\sqrt{\frac{\text{r}\mu}{n_1}}$, hence from Lemma \ref{lem:expection_bound-1} we have for $p$ large enough: \begin{equation} E({p}^{-1}||P_{U}P_{A^{(R)^{T}}}P_{U}-p P_{U}||_{2})<C\sqrt{\frac{log(n_1)r\mu}{p n_1}}\leq 1. \end{equation} For $\beta > 1$ which satisfy the lemma's requirement, take $\lambda=\sqrt{\frac{\beta}{\gamma}}$ where $\gamma$ as in Theorem \ref{theorem: talngrad_inequality-1}. We get that if $p>\frac{\mu log(n_1)r\beta}{n_1\gamma}$ then from Lemma \ref{lem:bound_Z-1} with probability of at least $1-3n_{1}^{-\beta}$ we have $Z\leq C\sqrt{\frac{log(n_1)r\mu}{p n_1}}+\frac{1}{\sqrt{\gamma}}\sqrt{\frac{log(n_1)r\mu\beta}{p n_1}}$. Taking $C_{R}=C+\frac{1}{\sqrt{\gamma}}$ finishes our proof.
nodes.statement_short: Write $P_UP_{A^{(R)T}}P_U$ as a Bernoulli sum of rank-one projections; bound its expectation (Lemma 5) and concentrate (Lemma 6).

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 2
nodes.statement: From Lemma \ref{lemma: uniqnes_MC} and using a union bound we have that with probability $>1-6min(n_1,n_2)^{-\beta}$, ${p^{(R)}}^{-1}||p^{(R)} \identity r-U^{T}A^{(R)^{T}}A^{(R)}U||_{2}<1$ and ${p^{(C)}}^{-1}||p^{(C)} \identity r-V^{T}A^{(C)}A^{(C)^{T}}V||_{2}<1$. Since the singular values of $p^{(R)} \identity r-U^{T}A^{(R)^{T}}A^{(R)}U$ are $|p^{(R)} -\sigma_{i}(U^{T}A^{(R)^{T}}A^{(R)}U)|$ for $1\leq i\leq r$, we have \begin{align} p^{(R)} -\sigma_{r}(U^{T}A^{(R)^{T}}A^{(R)}U)\leq \sigma_{1}(p^{(R)} \identity r-U^{T}A^{(R)^{T}}A^{(R)}U)<p^{(R)} \nonumber \\ \Rightarrow0<\sigma_{r}(U^{T}A^{(R)^{T}}A^{(R)}U) \end{align} and similarly for $V^{T}A^{(C)}A^{(C)^{T}}V$. Therefore $rank(A^{(R)}U)=rank(V^{T}A^{(C)})=r$ and $rank(A^{(R)} X)=rank(XA^{(C)})=r$ with probability $>1-6min(n_1,n_2)^{-\beta}$. From Lemma \ref{lem:hatX_is_X} we get $A^{(R)}X=A^{(R)}\hat{X}\,\quad XA^{(C)}=\hat{X}A^{(C)}$ and from Lemma \ref{lem:uniqness solution affine} we get $X=\hat{X}$ with probability $>1-6min(n_1,n_2)^{-\beta}$.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 4 and a union bound give $A^{(R)}U$, $V^TA^{(C)}$ of rank $r$; then Lemmas 2 and 1 give $\hat{X}=X$.

nodes.name: Szarek's bounds on extreme singular values of Gaussian matrices
nodes.statement: \cite{szarek1991condition} Let $A\in\matrixspace nk$ be a random matrix $A\overset{i.i.d.}{\sim} N(0,\frac{1}{n})$. Then, its largest and smallest singular values obey: \[ P\Big(\sigma_{1}(A)>1+\frac{\sqrt{k}}{\sqrt{n}}+t\Big) \text{\ensuremath{\le}}e^{-nt^{2}/2} \] \begin{equation} P\Big(\sigma_{k}(A)\leq1-\frac{\sqrt{k}}{\sqrt{n}}-t\Big) \text{\ensuremath{\le}}e^{-nt^{2}/2}. \end{equation}
assumptions: Let $A\in\matrixspace nk$ be a random matrix $A\overset{i.i.d.}{\sim} N(0,\frac{1}{n})$
nodes.label: Singular_Value_ranMatrix

nodes.name: Pseudoinverse norm bound for Gaussian matrices
nodes.statement: Let $A\in\matrixspace nk$ be a random matrix $A\overset{i.i.d.}{\sim} N(0,1)$ where $n\geq4k$, and let $\psuedoinv A$ be the Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse of $A$. Then \begin{equation} P\left(||\psuedoinv A||_{2}\leq\frac{6}{\sqrt{n}}\right)>1-e^{-n/18} \end{equation}
assumptions: Let $A\in\matrixspace nk$ be a random matrix $A\overset{i.i.d.}{\sim} N(0,1)$ where $n\geq4k$, and let $\psuedoinv A$ be the Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse of $A$
nodes.statement_short: For an $n\times k$ standard Gaussian matrix with $n\ge 4k$, $||A^\dagger||_2\le 6/\sqrt{n}$ w.p. $>1-e^{-n/18}$.
nodes.label: cor:psedo_inverse

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 2
nodes.statement: Since $\psuedoinv A$ is the pseudoinverse of $A$, $||\psuedoinv A||_{2}$=$\frac{1}{\sigma_{k}(A)}$ and from Theorem \ref{Singular_Value_ranMatrix} we get $\sigma_{k}(A)\geq\sqrt{n}-\sqrt{k}-t\sqrt{n}$ with probability $\geq 1-e^{nt^{2}/2}$ (notice the scaling by $\sqrt{n}$ of the entries of $A$ compared to Theorem \ref{Singular_Value_ranMatrix}). Therefore, if we take $n \geq 4k$ and $t=\frac{1}{3}$ we get \begin{equation} P\left(||\psuedoinv A||_{2}\leq\frac{6}{\sqrt{n}}\right)=P\left(\sigma_{k}(A)\geq\frac{\sqrt{n}}{6}\right) \geq 1-e^{-n/18}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: $||A^\dagger||_2=1/\sigma_k(A)$; apply Szarek's lower tail with $t=1/3$ and $n\ge 4k$.

nodes.name: Johnson-Lindenstrauss concentration for a finite set
nodes.statement: Let $Q$ to be a finite set of vectors in $\mathbb{R}^{n}$, let $\delta\in(0,1)$ and $k$ be an integer such that \begin{equation} \epsilon \equiv \sqrt{\frac{6log(2|Q|/\delta)}{k}} \leq 3 . \end{equation} Let $A\in\matrixspace kn$ be a random matrix with $A\overset{i.i.d.}{\sim} N(0,\frac{1}{k})$. Then, \begin{equation} P\left(max_{x\in Q}\left|\frac{||Ax||^{2}}{||x||^{2}}-1\right|\leq\epsilon\right)>1-\delta. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: A $k\times n$ Gaussian $N(0,1/k)$ matrix preserves squared norms of all vectors in $Q$ within $\epsilon$ w.p. $>1-\delta$.
nodes.label: lem:JL_Lemma

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 7
nodes.statement: Lemma \ref{lem:JL_Lemma} is a direct result of the Johnson-Lindenstrauss lemma \cite{dasgupta2003elementary} applied to each vector in $Q$ and using the union bound.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the Johnson-Lindenstrauss lemma to each vector of $Q$ and take a union bound.

nodes.name: One-pass low rank approximation algorithm (Halko-Martinsson-Tropp)
nodes.statement: Input: $A^{(R)},A^{(C)},B^{(R)},B^{(C)}$ \begin{enumerate} \item compute $Q^{(C)}R^{(C)}$ the QR decomposition of $B^{(C)}$, and $Q^{(R)}R^{(R)}$ the QR decomposition of $B^{(R)^{T}}$ \item Find the least-squares solution $Y=argmin_{C}||Q^{(C)}B^{(C)}-CQ^{(R)^{T}}B^{(R)^{T}}||_{F}$. \item Return the estimate $\hat{X}=Q^{(C)}YQ^{(R)^{T}}$. \end{enumerate} \protect\caption{}

nodes.statement: \mathbf{I}\equiv||(B^{(C,0)}-\svdtop{B^{(C)}}r)\psuedoinv{A_{V^{T}}^{(C)}}||_{F}

nodes.name: Term II
nodes.statement: \mathbf{II\equiv}||\hat{U}\psuedoinv{A_{\hat{U}}^{(R)}}A^{(R)}(B^{(C,0)}-\svdtop{B^{(C)}}r)\psuedoinv{A_{V^{T}}^{(C)}}||_{F}
nodes.label: eq:A2

nodes.name: Term III
nodes.statement: \mathbf{III\equiv}||\hat{U}\psuedoinv{A_{\hat{U}}^{(R)}}Z^{(R)}||_{F}.
nodes.label: eq:A3

nodes.name: First decomposition of $||X-\hat{X}||_F$
nodes.statement:
||X-\hat{X}||_{F}=
onumber \ ||X-\hat{U}(A_{\hat{U}}^{(R)^{T}}A_{\hat{U}}^{(R)})^{-1}A_{\hat{U}}^{(R)^{T}}(A^{(R)} X+Z^{(R)})||_{F}=
onumber \ ||X-\hat{U} \psuedoinv{A_{\hat{U}}^{(R)}} A^{(R)} X\: -\hat{U} \psuedoinv{A_{\hat{U}}^{(R)}} Z^{(R)}||_{F}\leq
onumber \ ||X-\hat{U} \psuedoinv{A_{\hat{U}}^{(R)}} A^{(R)} X||_{F}+\mathbf{III} \ 
onumber
nodes.label: eq:Firest_resonctruction of X

nodes.name: Identity $XA^{(C)}A_{V^T}^{(C)\dagger}V^T=X$
nodes.statement: XA^{(C)}\psuedoinv{A_{V^{T}}^{(C)}}V^{T}=U\Sigma V^{T}A^{(C)}\psuedoinv{A_{V^{T}}^{(C)}}V^{T}=U\Sigma V^{T}=X

nodes.name: Rewriting the first part via $B^{(C,0)}$
nodes.statement:
||X-\hat{U} \psuedoinv{A_{\hat{U}}^{(R)}} A^{(R)} X||_{F}=
onumber \ ||(\identity n-\hat{U}\psuedoinv{A_{\hat{U}}^{(R)}}A^{(R)})X||_{F}=
onumber \ ||(\identity n-\hat{U}\psuedoinv{A_{\hat{U}}^{(R)}}A^{(R)})XA^{(C)}\psuedoinv{A_{V^{T}}^{(C)}}V^{T}||_{F}=
onumber \ ||(\identity n-\hat{U}\psuedoinv{A_{\hat{U}}^{(R)}}A^{(R)})B^{(C,0)}\psuedoinv{A_{V^{T}}^{(C)}}||_{F}
nodes.label: eq:reconstruct_the_first_part1

nodes.name: Annihilation of $B^{(C)}_{(r)}$
nodes.statement: (\identity n-\hat{U}\psuedoinv{A_{\hat{U}}^{(R)}}A^{(R)})\svdtop{B^{(C)}}r= \svdtop{B^{(C)}}r-\hat{U}\psuedoinv{A_{\hat{U}}^{(R)}}A^{(R)}\hat{U}Y= \svdtop{B^{(C)}}r-\hat{U}Y=0 .
nodes.label: eq:L_and_U

nodes.name: Bound of the first part by I+II
nodes.statement: ||(\identity n-\hat{U}\psuedoinv{A_{\hat{U}}^{(R)}}A^{(R)})B^{(C,0)}\psuedoinv{A_{V^{T}}^{(C)}}||_{F}=\nonumber \\ ||(\identity n-\hat{U}\psuedoinv{A_{\hat{U}}^{(R)}}A^{(R)})(B^{(C,0)}-\svdtop{B^{(C)}}r)\psuedoinv{A_{V^{T}}^{(C)}}||_{F}\leq\nonumber \\ ||(B^{(C,0)}-\svdtop{B^{(C)}}r)\psuedoinv{A_{V^{T}}^{(C)}}||_{F} + ||\hat{U}\psuedoinv{A_{\hat{U}}^{(R)}}A^{(R)}(B^{(C,0)}-\svdtop{B^{(C)}}r)\psuedoinv{A_{V^{T}}^{(C)}}||_{F}=\mathbf{I+II}
nodes.label: eq:reconstruct_the_first_part

nodes.name: Matrix norm inequalities
nodes.statement: ||AB||_{2}\leq||A||_{2}||B||_{2} \nonumber \\ ||AB||_{F}\leq||A||_{F}||B||_{2} \nonumber \\ rank(A)\leqslant r \Rightarrow ||A||_{F}\leq\sqrt{r}||A||_{2}.
nodes.label: eq:three_matrix_inequalities

nodes.name: Rank bound for term I
nodes.statement: rank\left((B^{(C,0)}-\svdtop{B^{(C)}}r)\psuedoinv{A_{V^{T}}^{(C)}}\right)\leqslant rank\left(\psuedoinv{A_{V^{T}}^{(C)}}\right)\leqslant r .

nodes.name: Bound of I by spectral norms
nodes.statement: \mathbf{I}=||(B^{(C,0)}-\svdtop{B^{(C)}}r)\psuedoinv{A_{V^{T}}^{(C)}}||_{F}\leq \sqrt{r}||(B^{(C,0)}-\svdtop{B^{(C)}}r)||_{2}||\psuedoinv{A_{V^{T}}^{(C)}}||_{2}
nodes.label: eq:first_Bc_BCr

nodes.name: Term I bound with $6\sqrt{r/k}$
nodes.statement: \mathbf{I}\leq6\sqrt{\frac{r}{k}}||(B^{(C,0)}-\svdtop{B^{(C)}}r)||_{2}.
nodes.label: eq:BcBcrSQRT

nodes.name: Probabilistic bound on I
nodes.statement: P\Big(\mathbf{I}\leq C_{1}\sqrt{\frac{r}{k}}||Z^{(C)}||_{2} \Big) > 1-e^{-c_{1}k} .
nodes.label: eq:bound_A1

nodes.name: Bound on II by norms
nodes.statement: \mathbf{II=}||\hat{U}\psuedoinv{A_{\hat{U}}^{(R)}}A^{(R)}(B^{(C,0)}-\svdtop{B^{(C)}}r)\psuedoinv{A_{V^{T}}^{(C)}}||_{F}\leq \nonumber \nonumber \\ ||\psuedoinv{A_{\hat{U}}^{(R)}}||_{2}||A^{(R)}(B^{(C,0)}-\svdtop{B^{(C)}}r)||_{F} ||\psuedoinv{A_{V^{T}}^{(C)}}||_{2}.
nodes.label: eq:temp_equation2

nodes.name: Probabilistic bound on II (first)
nodes.statement: P \Big( \mathbf{II}\leq\frac{36}{k}||A^{(R)}(B^{(C,0)}-\svdtop{B^{(C)}}r)||_{F} \Big) > 1-2e^{-k/18}.
nodes.label: eq:Second(Bc-Br)

nodes.name: Bound on II via JL
nodes.statement: \mathbf{II}\leq\frac{36}{k}||A^{(R)}(B^{(C,0)}-\svdtop{B^{(C)}}r)||_{F}\leq \nonumber \\ \frac{36\sqrt{2k}}{k}||(B^{(C,0)}-\svdtop{B^{(C)}}r)||_{F}\leq 36\sqrt{4\frac{r}{k}}||(B^{(C,0)}-\svdtop{B^{(C)}}r)||_{2}.
nodes.label: eq:secondBcBcrSQRT

nodes.name: Probabilistic bound on II
nodes.statement: P \Big (\mathbf{II}\leq C_{2}||Z^{(C)}||_{2} \Big) > 1-3e^{-c_2k} .
nodes.label: eq:bound_A2

nodes.name: Bound on III
nodes.statement: \mathbf{III=}||\hat{U}\psuedoinv{A_{\hat{U}}^{(R)}}Z^{(R)}||_{F}= ||\psuedoinv{A_{\hat{U}}^{(R)}}Z^{(R)}||_{F}\leq \nonumber \\ \sqrt{r}||\psuedoinv{A_{\hat{U}}^{(R)}}Z^{(R)}||_{2}\leq \sqrt{r}||\psuedoinv{A_{\hat{U}}^{(R)}}||_{2}||Z^{(R)}||_{2}\leq\frac{6\sqrt{r}}{\sqrt{k}}||Z^{(R)}||_{2} .
nodes.label: eq:Z(R)_bound

nodes.name: Probabilistic bound on III
nodes.statement: P\Big(\mathbf{III}\leq C_{3}||Z^{(R)}||_{2} \Big) > 1-e^{-c_{3}k}.
nodes.label: eq:bound_A3

nodes.name: Basis $\hat{U}$ of the column space of $B^{(C)}$
nodes.statement:
Compute a basis (of size $r$) to the column space of $B^{(C)}$ using Gaussian elimination,
represented as the columns of a matrix $\hat{U} \in \matrixspace {n_{1}}r $.

nodes.name: Solve the linear systems for $Y$
nodes.statement:
Solve the linear system $B_{\bullet j}^{(R)}=A^{(R)}\hat{U}Y_{\bullet j}$ for
each $j=1,..,n_2$ and write the solutions as a matrix $Y=Y_{\bullet1}...Y_{\bullet n_{2}}$.

nodes.name: Output $\hat{U}Y$
nodes.statement: Output $\hat{X}=\hat{U}Y$

nodes.name: Top-$r$ left singular vectors of $B^{(C)}$
nodes.statement: Compute $\hat{U}$, the $r$ largest left singular vectors of $B^{(C)}$, ($\hat{U}$ is a basis for the columns space of $B^{(C)}_{(r)}$).

nodes.name: Least squares for $\hat{Y}$
nodes.statement_short: Least-squares fit of row measurements given $\hat{U}$, with closed form when $A^{(R)}\hat{U}$ has rank $r$.
nodes.label: eq:close_formula_alg2

nodes.name: Row estimate $\hat{X}^{(R)}$
nodes.statement: Compute the estimate $\hat{X}^{(R)}=\hat{U}\hat{Y}$.

nodes.name: Symmetric column estimate $\hat{X}^{(C)}$
nodes.statement:
Repeat steps 1-3, replacing the roles of columns and rows to get
an estimate $\hat{X}^{(C)}$.
nodes.statement_short: Repeat steps 1-3 with rows and columns swapped.

nodes.name: Keep the lower-loss estimate
nodes.statement: Set $\hat{X} = argmin_{\hat{X}^{(R)},\hat{X}^{(C)}} \mathcal{\mathcal{{F}}}(X)$, for the loss $\mathcal{\mathcal{{F}}}(X)$ given in eq. (\ref{eq:losses_function}).
nodes.statement_short: Choose between $\hat{X}^{(R)}$ and $\hat{X}^{(C)}$ by the loss $\mathcal{F}$.

nodes.name: QR decompositions of $B^{(C)}$ and $B^{(R)T}$
nodes.statement:
compute $Q^{(C)}R^{(C)}$ the QR decomposition of $B^{(C)}$,
and $Q^{(R)}R^{(R)}$ the QR decomposition of $B^{(R)^{T}}$

nodes.name: Least-squares core $Y$
nodes.statement: Find the least-squares solution $Y=argmin_{C}||Q^{(C)}B^{(C)}-CQ^{(R)^{T}}B^{(R)^{T}}||_{F}$.

nodes.name: Return $Q^{(C)}YQ^{(R)T}$
nodes.statement: Return the estimate $\hat{X}=Q^{(C)}YQ^{(R)^{T}}$.

nodes.name: Factored loss $\mathcal{L}(W,S)$
nodes.statement: The gradient descent stage is performed directly in the space of rank $r$ matrices, using the decomposition $\hat{X}$=$WS$ where $W\in\matrixspace{n_{1}}r$ and $S\in\matrixspace r{n_{2}}$ and computing the gradient of the loss as a function of $W$ and $S$, \begin{equation} \mathcal{\mathcal{{L}}}(W,S) = \mathcal{\mathcal{{F}}}(WS) = ||A^{(R)} WS-B^{(R)}||_{F}^{2} + ||WSA^{(C)}-B^{(C)}||_{F}^{2}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Parametrize $\hat{X}=WS$ and define the factored loss.

nodes.name: Start from the SVLS estimate
nodes.statement: We want to minimize eq. (\ref{eq:loss_function_W_S}) but the loss $\mathcal{\mathcal{{L}}}$ isn't convex and therefore gradient descent may fail to converge to a global optimum. We propose $\hat{X}$ (the output of SVLS\!) as a starting point which may be close enough to enable gradient descent to converge to the global optimum, and in addition may accelerate convergence.
nodes.statement_short: Initialize gradient descent at the SVLS output.

nodes.name: Gradients in $W$ and $S$
nodes.statement: The gradient of $\mathcal{\mathcal{{L}}}$ is (using the chain rule) $$ \frac{\partial \mathcal{\mathcal{{L}}}}{\partial W}= 2 \Big[ A^{(R)^{T}}(A^{(R)} WS-B^{(R)})S^{T}+(WSA^{(C)}-B^{(C)})A^{(C)^{T}}S^{T} \Big] $$ \begin{equation} \frac{\partial \mathcal{\mathcal{{L}}}}{\partial S}= 2 \Big[ W^{T}A^{(R)^{T}}(A^{(R)} WS-B^{(R)})+W^{T}(WSA^{(C)}-B^{(C)})A^{(C)^{T}} \Big] \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Chain-rule gradients of $\mathcal{L}$ in $W$ and $S$.

nodes.name: Elbow estimate from $B^{(C)}$
nodes.statement: For the noisy case we estimate $rank(X)$ from $B^{(C)},B^{(R)}$. We use the popular elbow method to estimate $rank(B^{(C)})$ in the following way \begin{equation} \hat{r}^{(C)}=argmax_{i\in[k^{(C)}-1]}\left(\frac{\sigma_{i}(B^{(C)})}{\sigma_{i+1}(B^{(C)})}\right) \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Largest ratio of consecutive singular values of $B^{(C)}$.

nodes.name: Average with the row estimate
nodes.statement: We compute similarly $\hat{r}^{(R)}$ from $B^{(R)}$ and take the average as our rank estimator, $\hat{r}=round\left(\frac{\hat{r}^{(C)}+\hat{r}^{(C)}}{2}\right)$.
nodes.statement_short: Same for $B^{(R)}$; round the average.

nodes.name: Gaussian noise has spectral norm $O(\tau\sqrt{n})$
nodes.statement: Theorem \ref{thm:the_noisy_case} applies for any $Z^{(C)}$ and $Z^{(R)}$. If $k\leq n$ and $Z^{(R)},Z^{(C)}\overset{i.i.d.}{\sim} N(0,\tau^{2})$, then from eq. (\ref{eq:matrix_singular_values}) we get $max(||Z^{(R)}||_{2},||Z^{(C)}||_{2}) \leq 4\tau \sqrt{n}$ with probability $1-e^{-2n}$.
nodes.statement_short: Bound $||Z||_2\le 4\tau\sqrt{n}$ via Szarek's inequality.

nodes.name: Conclude the corollary
nodes.statement: We therefore get the next Corollary for i.i.d. additive Gaussian noise:
nodes.statement_short: Substitute into Theorem 3.

nodes.name: Common column space
nodes.statement: First, $rank(X_{2}A^{(C)})=rank(X_{1}A^{(C)})=r$ and similarly $rank(A^{(R)}X_{2})= \allowbreak rank(A^{(R)}X_{1}) \allowbreak = \allowbreak r$. Since $span(X_{1}A^{(C)}),span(X_{2}A^{(C)})$ are subspaces of $span(X_{1}), \allowbreak span(X_{2})$ respectively, and $dim(span(X_{2})) \leq r$ we get $span(X_{2})=span(X_{2}A^{(C)}) \allowbreak =span(X_{1}A^{(C)})=span(X_{1})$, and we define $U\in\orthomatrixspace{n_{1}}r$ a basis for this subspace.
nodes.statement_short: Both have full-rank column measurements, so their column spaces coincide; take a basis $U$.

nodes.name: Factor through $U$
nodes.statement: For $X_{1},X_{2}$ there are $Y_{1},Y_{2}\in\matrixspace r{n_{2}}$ such that $X_{1}=UY_{1},X_{2}=UY_{2}$. Therefore $A^{(R)}UY_{1}=A^{(R)}UY_{2}$.
nodes.statement_short: Write $X_i=UY_i$; row measurements agree.

nodes.name: Invertibility gives $Y_1=Y_2$
nodes.statement: Since $rank(A^{(R)}UY_{1})=r$ and $U\in\orthomatrixspace{n_{1}}r$ we get $rank(A^{(R)} U)=r$, hence the matrix $U^{T}A^{(R)^{T}}A^{(R)}U$ is invertible, which gives $Y_{1}=Y_{2}$, and therefore $X_{1}=UY_{1}=UY_{2}=X_{2}$.
nodes.statement_short: $A^{(R)}U$ has rank $r$, so $Y_1=Y_2$ and $X_1=X_2$.

nodes.name: $\hat{U}$ spans $span(X)$
nodes.statement: $span(XA^{(C)})\subseteq span(X)$ and $rank(XA^{(C)})=rank(X)=r$, therefore $span(XA^{(C)})=span(X)$ and $\hat{U}$ from stage 1 in Algorithm \ref{alg:noiseless_case} is a basis for $span(X)$.
nodes.statement_short: The column measurements span the column space of $X$.

nodes.name: Factor $X=\hat{U}Y$
nodes.statement: We can write $X=\hat{U} Y$ for some matrix $Y\in\mathbb{R}_{r\times n_{2}}$. Since $rank(A^{(R)}\hat{U}Y)=rank(\hat{U})=r$, we have $rank(A^{(R)}\hat{U})=r$.
nodes.statement_short: Write $X=\hat{U}Y$; $A^{(R)}\hat{U}$ has rank $r$.

nodes.name: Verify both equalities
nodes.statement:
Thus eq. (ef{eq:algorithm1}) gives $\hat{X}$ in closed form and we get:  egin{align} A^{(R)}\hat{X}=A^{(R)}\hat{U}[\hat{U}^{T}A^{(R)^{T}}A^{(R)}\hat{U}]^{-1}\hat{U}^{T}A^{(R)^{T}}B^{(R,0)}= 
onumber\ A^{(R)}\hat{U}[\hat{U}^{T}A^{(R)^{T}}A^{(R)}\hat{U}]^{-1}\hat{U}^{T}A^{(R)^{T}}A^{(R)}\hat{U}Y= 
onumber\ A^{(R)}\hat{U}Y=A^{(R)} X . \end{align} \vspace{-1.0cm}  egin{align} \hat{X}A^{(C)}=\hat{U}[\hat{U}^{T}A^{(R)^{T}}A^{(R)}\hat{U}]^{-1}\hat{U}^{T}A^{(R)^{T}}A^{(R)} XA^{(C)}= 
onumber\ \hat{U}[\hat{U}^{T}A^{(R)^{T}}A^{(R)}\hat{U}]^{-1}\hat{U}^{T}A^{(R)^{T}}A^{(R)}\hat{U}YA^{(C)}= 
onumber\ \hat{U}YA^{(C)}=XA^{(C)} . \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Substitute in the closed form to get (16) and (17).

nodes.name: $V^TA^{(C)}$ has rank $r$ a.s.
nodes.statement: Let $U\Sigma V^{T}$ be the $SVD$ of $X$. From Lemma \ref{lem:unitary_normal} the elements of the matrix $V^T A^{(C)}$ have a continuous Gaussian distribution and since the measure of low rank matrices is zero and $k^{(C)}\geq r$ we get that $P(rank(V^{T} A^{(C)})=r)=1$.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 3: $V^TA^{(C)}$ is Gaussian, hence of rank $r$ a.s.

nodes.name: Measurements have rank $r$ a.s.
nodes.statement: Since $B^{(C)}=U\Sigma V^{T} A^{(C)}$ we get $P(rank(B^{(C)})=rank(U\Sigma V^{T} A^{(C)})=r)=1$. In the same way $P(rank(B^{(R)})=r)=1$.
nodes.statement_short: Hence $B^{(C)}$ and $B^{(R)}$ have rank $r$ a.s.

nodes.name: Combine Lemmas 1 and 2
nodes.statement: Combining Lemma \ref{lem:hatX_is_X} with Lemma \ref{lem:uniqness solution affine} give us the required result.
nodes.statement_short: Lemmas 2 and 1 give $\hat{X}=X$.

nodes.name: $Z$ as a supremum
nodes.statement: We know that $Z=||Y||_{2}=sup_{f_{1},f_{2}} \langle f_{1},Yf_{2} \rangle =sup_{f_{1},f_{2}}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\langle f_{1,}Y_{i}f_{2} \rangle$, where the supremum is taken over a countable set of unit vectors $f_{1},f_{2}\in F_{V}$.
nodes.statement_short: Express the spectral norm as a supremum over unit vectors.

nodes.name: Function class with zero mean
nodes.statement: Let $F$ be the set of all functions $f$ such that $f(Y)= \langle f_{1},Yf_{2} \rangle$ for some unit vectors $f_{1},f_{2}\in F_{V}$. For every $f\in F$ and $i\in[n]$ we have $E(f(Y_{i}))=0$.
nodes.statement_short: Define the function class; each $f(Y_i)$ is centered.

nodes.name: Uniform bound
nodes.statement: From the incoherence of $U$ we conclude that \begin{equation} |f(Y_{i})| = p^{-1} |r_{i}-p| \times | \langle f_{1},P_{U}(e_{i}) \rangle | \times | \langle P_{U}(e_{i}),f_{2} \rangle | \leq p^{-1} ||P_{U}(e_{i})||^{2} \leq p^{-1}\frac{r}{n}\mu. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Incoherence bounds $|f(Y_i)|\le p^{-1}\mu r/n$.

nodes.name: Variance bound
nodes.statement: In addition \[ E (f^{2}(Y_{i})) =p^{-1}(1-p) \langle f_{1},P_{U}(e_{i}) \rangle^{2} \langle P_{U}(e_{i}),f_{2} \rangle^{2} \leq \] \begin{equation} p^{-1}||P_{U}(e_{i})||^{2}| \langle P_{U}(e_{i}),f_{2} \rangle^2 |\leq p^{-1}\frac{r}{n}\mu| \langle P_{U}(e_{i}),f_{2} \rangle|^{2}. \end{equation} Since $\sum_{i=1}^{n}| \langle P_{U}(e_{i}),f_{2} \rangle|^{2}=\sum_{i=1}^{n}| \langle e_{i},P_{U}(f_{2}) \rangle |^{2}=||P_{U}(f_{2})||^{2} \leq 1$, we get $\sum_{i=1}^{n} E (f^{2}(Y_{i})) \leq p^{-1}\frac{r}{n}\mu.$
nodes.statement_short: Sum of variances is at most $p^{-1}\mu r/n$.

nodes.name: Apply Talagrand
nodes.statement: We can take $B=2p^{-1}\frac{r}{n}\mu$ and $t=\lambda\sqrt{\frac{\mu rlog(n)}{pn}}$ and from Theorem \ref{theorem: talngrad_inequality-1}: \begin{equation} P(|Z-E(Z)|\geq t) \leq 3exp\left(\frac{-t}{KB}log(1+\frac{t}{2})\right) \leq 3exp\left(\frac{-tlog(2)}{KB}min(1,\frac{t}{2})\right) \end{equation} where the last inequality is due to the fact that for every $u>0$ we have $log(1+u)\geq log(2)min(1,u)$. Taking $\gamma=-log(2)/K$ finishes our proof.
nodes.statement_short: Talagrand's inequality with $\log(1+u)\ge\log 2\min(1,u)$.

nodes.name: Expand in the standard basis
nodes.statement: (Lemma \ref{lemma: uniqnes_MC}) Represent any vector $w\in R^{n_1}$ in the standard basis as $w=\sum_{i=1}^{n_1} \langle w,e_{i} \rangle e_{i}$. Therefore $P_{U}(w)=\sum_{i=1}^{n_1} \langle P_{U}(w),e_{i} \rangle e_{i}=\sum_{i=1}^{n_1} \langle w,P_{U}(e_{i}) \rangle e_{i}$.
nodes.statement_short: Write $P_U(w)$ in the standard basis.

nodes.name: Recall the sampling variables
nodes.statement: Recall the $r_i$ Bernoulli variables which determine if $e_i$ is included as a row of $A^{(R)}$ as in Section \ref{sec:Preliminaries-and-Notations} and define $Y_i$ and $Z$ as in Lemma \ref{lem:bound_Z-1}.
nodes.statement_short: Recall $r_i$ and define $Y_i$, $Z$ as in Lemma 6.

nodes.name: Sum of rank-one projections and expectation bound
nodes.statement: We get \begin{align} P_{A^{(R)^{T}}}P_{U}(w)=\sum_{i=1}^{n_1}r_{i} \langle w,P_{U}(e_{i}) \rangle e_{i}\Longrightarrow \nonumber \\ P_{U}P_{A^{(R)^{T}}}P_{U}(w)=\sum_{i=1}^{n_1}r_{i} \langle w,P_{U}(e_{i}) \rangle P_{U}(e_{i}) \end{align} In other words the matrix $P_{U}P_{A^{(R)^{T}}}P_{U}$ is given by \begin{equation} P_{U}P_{A^{(R)^{T}}}P_{U} = \sum_{i=1}^{n_1} r_{i}P_{U}(e_{i})\otimes P_{U}(e_{i}) \end{equation} $U$ is $\mu-$incoherent, thus $max_{i\in[n_1]}||P_{U}(e_{i})||\leq\sqrt{\frac{\text{r}\mu}{n_1}}$, hence from Lemma \ref{lem:expection_bound-1} we have for $p$ large enough: \begin{equation} E({p}^{-1}||P_{U}P_{A^{(R)^{T}}}P_{U}-p P_{U}||_{2})<C\sqrt{\frac{log(n_1)r\mu}{p n_1}}\leq 1. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: $P_UP_{A^{(R)T}}P_U=\sum_i r_iP_Ue_i\otimes P_Ue_i$; incoherence and Lemma 5 bound its expected deviation.

nodes.name: Concentration and constant
nodes.statement: For $\beta > 1$ which satisfy the lemma's requirement, take $\lambda=\sqrt{\frac{\beta}{\gamma}}$ where $\gamma$ as in Theorem \ref{theorem: talngrad_inequality-1}. We get that if $p>\frac{\mu log(n_1)r\beta}{n_1\gamma}$ then from Lemma \ref{lem:bound_Z-1} with probability of at least $1-3n_{1}^{-\beta}$ we have $Z\leq C\sqrt{\frac{log(n_1)r\mu}{p n_1}}+\frac{1}{\sqrt{\gamma}}\sqrt{\frac{log(n_1)r\mu\beta}{p n_1}}$. Taking $C_{R}=C+\frac{1}{\sqrt{\gamma}}$ finishes our proof.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 6 with $\lambda=\sqrt{\beta/\gamma}$; set $C_R=C+1/\sqrt{\gamma}$.

nodes.name: Apply Lemma 4 to rows and columns
nodes.statement: From Lemma \ref{lemma: uniqnes_MC} and using a union bound we have that with probability $>1-6min(n_1,n_2)^{-\beta}$, ${p^{(R)}}^{-1}||p^{(R)} \identity r-U^{T}A^{(R)^{T}}A^{(R)}U||_{2}<1$ and ${p^{(C)}}^{-1}||p^{(C)} \identity r-V^{T}A^{(C)}A^{(C)^{T}}V||_{2}<1$.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 4 for rows and columns plus union bound.

nodes.name: Smallest singular value positive
nodes.statement: Since the singular values of $p^{(R)} \identity r-U^{T}A^{(R)^{T}}A^{(R)}U$ are $|p^{(R)} -\sigma_{i}(U^{T}A^{(R)^{T}}A^{(R)}U)|$ for $1\leq i\leq r$, we have \begin{align} p^{(R)} -\sigma_{r}(U^{T}A^{(R)^{T}}A^{(R)}U)\leq \sigma_{1}(p^{(R)} \identity r-U^{T}A^{(R)^{T}}A^{(R)}U)<p^{(R)} \nonumber \\ \Rightarrow0<\sigma_{r}(U^{T}A^{(R)^{T}}A^{(R)}U) \end{align} and similarly for $V^{T}A^{(C)}A^{(C)^{T}}V$.
nodes.statement_short: Hence $\sigma_r(U^TA^{(R)T}A^{(R)}U)>0$.

nodes.name: Full rank measurements
nodes.statement: Therefore $rank(A^{(R)}U)=rank(V^{T}A^{(C)})=r$ and $rank(A^{(R)} X)=rank(XA^{(C)})=r$ with probability $>1-6min(n_1,n_2)^{-\beta}$.
nodes.statement_short: So $A^{(R)}X$ and $XA^{(C)}$ have rank $r$.

nodes.name: Conclude by Lemmas 2 and 1
nodes.statement: From Lemma \ref{lem:hatX_is_X} we get $A^{(R)}X=A^{(R)}\hat{X}\,\quad XA^{(C)}=\hat{X}A^{(C)}$ and from Lemma \ref{lem:uniqness solution affine} we get $X=\hat{X}$ with probability $>1-6min(n_1,n_2)^{-\beta}$.
nodes.statement_short: Lemmas 2 and 1 give $X=\hat{X}$.

nodes.name: Split off the noise term
nodes.statement:
We represent $||X-\hat{X}||_{F}$ as follows  egin{align} ||X-\hat{X}||_{F}=
onumber \ ||X-\hat{U}(A_{\hat{U}}^{(R)^{T}}A_{\hat{U}}^{(R)})^{-1}A_{\hat{U}}^{(R)^{T}}(A^{(R)} X+Z^{(R)})||_{F}=
onumber \ ||X-\hat{U} \psuedoinv{A_{\hat{U}}^{(R)}} A^{(R)} X\: -\hat{U} \psuedoinv{A_{\hat{U}}^{(R)}} Z^{(R)}||_{F}\leq
onumber \ ||X-\hat{U} \psuedoinv{A_{\hat{U}}^{(R)}} A^{(R)} X||_{F}+\mathbf{III} \ 
onumber \end{align} where we have used the triangle inequality.
nodes.statement_short: Substitute $B^{(R)}=A^{(R)}X+Z^{(R)}$; triangle inequality isolates III.

nodes.name: Rewrite through $B^{(C,0)}$
nodes.statement:

(\ref{eq:A1}) we get a bound on $\mathbf{I}$ for some absolute constants $C_{1},c_{1}$: \begin{equation} P\Big(\mathbf{I}\leq C_{1}\sqrt{\frac{r}{k}}||Z^{(C)}||_{2} \Big) > 1-e^{-c_{1}k} . \end{equation}
